title: SLO contract gating for multiregion inference and throttle matrix
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define a per-endpoint & per-model SLO/SLI declaration format and automated gating that ties error-budget state to multiregion failover, circuit breaker tripping, and priority load-shedding. The goal is a deterministic, auditable policy so console rollouts and routing decisions can act consistently across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLO declaration format persisted in service config and visible in Console for each endpoint and model variant
Automated gate that transitions endpoints through NORMAL -> PROTECT -> DEGRADED -> EVACUATE states based on error-budget burn and regional signals
Circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shedding matrix implemented in routing service and verified with simulated traffic tests
Dashboards and alerts for SLO burn-rate, protected slice occupancy, and cross-region failover latency; runbook updated
decisions: SLOs will be two-part: an availability/latency SLI (percentile) and a quality SLI (prompt-set regression pass rate). Both contribute to a single normalized error budget for gating
Per-endpoint SLOs default to: P95 latency < 220ms, P99 latency < 700ms, availability (5xx+timeout) >= 99.95% for hosted tier. Enterprise/dedicated routes can opt-in to tighter or looser contracts
Error-budget burn uses 24h rolling window with weighted burn for tail latencies; cross-region borrowing allowed but requires escrow reconciliation
Circuit-breaker tiers: soft (adaptive throttling at 85% burn), hard (reject at 95% burn), and regional ejection when regional burn > 70% and cross-region capacity available

Load-shedding decisions prioritize routes via a per-route priority score, then by customer tier, then by model pinned variant. Graceful degradation uses pinned fallback variants rather than hard rejects where possible
implementation_plan: 1) Schema: design SLO declaration JSON schema and storage location in endpoint config (config-service)
2) Orchestration: implement finite-state machine in route-manager to map error-budget signals to state transitions and publish state via service discovery
3) Routing: extend router to interpret state and apply throttles/circuit decisions (accept/queue/evict) and variant substitution rules
4) Observability: add SLO burn-rate aggregator and dashboards (Grafana) + two PagerDuty alerts: SLO-BURN-WARN and SLO-BURN-CRIT
5) Testing: create traffic rehearsal harness (k6 + recorded workloads) to validate transitions and verify rollback paths
6) Docs: update Console rollout gating docs and runbooks; add examples for Dedicated and Private deployments
7) Rollout: staged deployment in us-west-2 canary, then global rollout with dark-launch monitoring
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff meeting with PM/Design/Routing. Agreed to combine latency and quality into a single budget metric to simplify gating
2025-01-20: Schema draft posted to Confluence. Design asked to show Console UX for state visibility (DES-1023 linked)
2025-01-24: Prototype FSM implemented in route-manager branch feat/slo-fsm. Unit tests for state transitions added
2025-01-28: Observability PO approved aggregation job; Grafana panel skeleton created. Need infra quota request for aggregation lambdas
2025-02-01: Integration test failing under bursty traffic—identified race between cache eviction and state publish. Added mutex around state update in route-manager (PR 1291)
review_feedback: PM (Lina Ortega): tie 'degraded' state to visible console banner and automated rollback when customer-impact 'high'
Design (Sofia Patel): prefer color-coded SLO state badges and 'why degraded' drilldown showing exact error-budget math
Security (Rahul Menon): flagged potential info leak in public metrics endpoint; recommended auth gating for per-tenant SLO payloads
SRE (Karan Iyer): suggested increasing soft throttle aggressiveness for memory-bound models to reduce eviction churn
risks: Incorrect normalization of quality and latency into single budget could make low-quality regressions look masked by low latency
Cross-region borrowing without strict reconciliation could hide persistent regional issues and delay capacity provisioning
Aggressive automated failover might increase egress costs (multi-region replication of models) if not bounded
Private deployments may not support centralized aggregation; need local-only fallback mode
test_plan: Unit: state machine transition table tests for NORMAL/PROTECT/DEGRADED/EVACUATE
Integration: k6 replay of 7 production traffic traces across two regions with simulated 50% P99 latency spike
Chaos: kill regional routing agents and validate failover and debt repayment behavior
E2E: console visibility test and alert firing verification in staging
rollout_plan: Dark launch: enable FSM publishing but no enforcement in us-west-2 for 48h; monitor burn rate metrics
Canary enforcement: enable throttling for 10% of traffic in us-west-2, observe 72h
Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over three days if no critical alerts
Enterprise opt-out window: notify Dedicated customers and allow a 7-day opt-out before enforcement
monitoring_alerts: REGION-EJECT: regional error-budget > 70% and failover actions initiated
